title: Rehearsal takes and how Russell sessions differed from Armstrong's
summary: Russell's sessions gave three or four takes described as rehearsal, and he never knew about alternate takes; Russell's band knew its numbers unlike the Armstrong sessions.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: But now, the Russell band, you took down mostly everything on the first or second take. I mean, you didn't...

No. We had four takes. Three and four takes. Because see, we were... They had told us these takes were just rehearsal. "You're rehearsing on these takes." And then you played what you call a Master. That's why you might hear anything on some of them other takes. Because we were told in the studio that that was rehearsal.
I guess the engineers were getting their levels.
Well, I don't know, you know... I mean, they came out way later. Like, when I heard some of your records, some numbers we recorded, and I know it wasn't the master that come out.
That's right. And I have never heard of no alternate takes.
But you never had any all day doing one thing.
I mean, when you went into the studio with the Russell Band, you made several numbers at each session.
No, we did all day on "Can't Give You Anything But Love."
Yeah, but that was with Louis.
No, that was the same thing.
But I mean before Louis, when you did the recordings before Louis had fronted the band, you didn't seem to have any problems.
No. We knew what it was going to do.

Most of the numbers we knew what we were going to do. But when you were down there with Louis, you'd never know what you're going to record. Because somebody would walk in with anything, and he would say "Yes," and here you would be.
